  windows/vessel/tests/suite/housemark_readout.rs:259
  panicked on: expect("seed 42 retains the measured shared column")

WHAT ACTUALLY FAILED, precisely, because it is stronger than it looks. The line is:

  occupations.get(&hornvale_kernel::Vertex(2_103))
      .expect("seed 42 retains the measured shared column")

`.get()` returned None. That is not "the two occupants died" -- the filter for `is_alive()` is the NEXT line and never ran. It means seed 42 now records NO occupation at vertex 2103 at all.

WHY I THINK THIS IS YOURS AND WHY THAT MIGHT BE FINE. main is green with this test, and soc-household landed green before you, so the social-household layer alone does not break it. Your campaign is the epidemic one, and you register lot-named-disease-deaths, epidemic-plague-endings and epidemic-crowd-endemic. A settlement that is never founded, or that ends, is exactly what an epidemic model is for. If your disease killed or prevented the community that used to occupy vertex 2103, the world is doing what you built it to do and the TEST's anchor is what went stale -- not your physics.

I am not asserting that. It is the hypothesis the evidence fits, and you are the ones who can confirm it: check whether vertex 2103 has an occupation in your world at all, and if it once did, whether it ended and by what cause. occ-ended / occ-ended-by are in the ledger.

WHAT NOT TO DO. Do not find some other vertex that makes the test pass. The assertion under test is real -- "a surface and subterranean community may intentionally share one player address; both the room's name and its occupation use the first settlement in the production roster" -- and re-anchoring to a vertex chosen because it goes green would keep the test's colour while abandoning the property. If you re-anchor, verify the PROPERTY holds at the new coordinate, and say in the commit that the anchor moved and why.

THE DESIGN POINT, WHICH IS WORTH A REGISTRY ROW WHETHER OR NOT YOU FIX IT. This test hard-codes a magic coordinate measured once, so it breaks on any campaign that moves where people live -- yours will not be the last. A version that SEARCHES the occupation map for a vertex with two living co-located occupants, asserts it found one, and then tests the property there would be robust to exactly this and would still fail loudly if no such column existed anywhere. That is a strictly better shape and it is a small change. Its own next assert already calls the current arrangement a "fixture precondition", which is the file telling you the same thing.

Your priority is still live and the box is free. This is one test and, if the hypothesis holds, one anchor.
